Transcripts available: full-year 2024 (2025-02-20), Q1 2025 (2025-05-09), Q2 2025 (2025-08-14), Q3 2025 (2025-11-13) and full-year 2025 (2026-02-19). The Q1 and Q2 2026 calls are not in the bundle; for 2026 we rely on FMP's reported statements and dated company announcements.*

**The takeaway first.** Zealand is a development-stage peptide company that turned two partnerships into one of the strongest balance sheets in European biotech. At today's price the market values the whole company at roughly its cash and receivables, so investors are paying close to nothing for a 50/50 profit share in petrelintide (an amylin analog - a hormone mimic that reduces appetite with fewer stomach side effects than GLP-1 drugs) and a royalty on Boehringer Ingelheim's survodutide. The catch is that the 2026 clinical data have been good-but-not-great, and the cash will be spent on an expensive Phase 3 program before any product revenue arrives.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC
- **Early 2025 (FY2024 call, 2025-02-20):** the story was ambition. Management called 2024 "a transformational year" and said Zealand wanted to "become a key player in the growing obesity market", while still carrying rare-disease programs (congenital hyperinsulinism, short bowel syndrome). Cash was about DKK 9 billion and management had stopped guiding on cash runway ("you don't really guide on the runway anymore").
- **2025 (Q1-Q3 calls):** the Roche deal (up to about $5.3 billion, $1.65 billion upfront, US/EU profit split 50/50) re-framed Zealand from a stand-alone developer to a partner-funded co-owner. The FY2025 numbers show it: revenue DKK 9.21 billion and net income DKK 6.46 billion, almost entirely the Roche upfront.
- **Now (FY2025 call, 2026-02-19):** the language shifted from "transformational" to "the most defining and catalyst rich year" - 2026 was meant to prove the assets. Management set an explicit bar: petrelintide should show it can reach "approximately 15% to 20% body weight reduction in longer-term Phase III trials" with tolerability "significantly better" than incretin drugs. The pitch broadened into an AI-and-automation research hub in Boston and "more than 10 candidates into the clinic" over five years - a widening of scope just as the core asset entered its proof year.
- **What was quietly de-emphasised:** rare disease barely features in the FY2025 call; the stand-alone commercial build-out language of 2024 gave way to partner-led commercialisation.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)
| Management claim | What the numbers / dated facts show | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Very sufficient cash position" (2025-02-20) | Cash and securities DKK 14.46 billion plus DKK 3.82 billion of Roche receivables at 2026-06-30, total debt DKK 0.41 billion | Corroborated - stronger than claimed |
| Roche partnership "delivered on everything we had hoped for" (2026-02-19) | Q2 2026 revenue DKK 4.49 billion (a milestone tied to the Phase 3 decision announced 2026-04-29); Phase 3 program started 2026-09-22 | Corroborated |
| Petrelintide on course for 15-20% weight loss with better tolerability | Phase 2 ZUPREME-1 (2026-03-05) about 10.7% at 28 weeks versus 1.7% on placebo; ZUPREME-2 in type 2 diabetes (2026-10-07) up to 9.2% versus 2.0% | Unproven - single digits to low double digits so far, the 15-20% rests on longer trials |
| Survodutide "preferred therapy for a large population" | SYNCHRONIZE-1 16.6% weight loss (ADA, June 2026); SYNCHRONIZE-2 up to 13.1% at 76 weeks with 18% stopping for stomach side effects (2026-10-01) | Competitive but not class-leading |
| Earnings power | Recurring revenue only DKK 34 million in Q1 2026 versus DKK 563 million of quarterly operating costs; trailing free cash flow minus DKK 1.80 billion; return on invested capital about minus 25% | The reported 2.6x price-to-free-cash-flow is a milestone artifact, not earnings |

The screener's cheapness signals (discounted cash flow value DKK 522.8, price/FCF 2.6x) are built on one-off partnership cash and should be disregarded. The honest valuation anchor is the balance sheet plus a risk-weighted pipeline.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY
**Stable to slightly declining in specificity.** 2025 calls were offensive ("key player", stand-alone ambition). The FY2025 call was still confident but hedged on differentiation: asked how petrelintide would stand against other amylin drugs, the CEO said "It is too early for us to share our thoughts about the ultimate differentiation" (2026-02-19). Specific numeric targets (15-20%) were given, which helps accountability; but the subsequent readouts fell short of what the market read into them.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY
- Timelines: delivered. Phase 2 readout in Q1 2026 (done 2026-03-05), Phase 3 start "later this year" (done 2026-09-22), survodutide Phase 3 data through 2026 (done, June and October).
- Efficacy expectations: under-delivered against the investor read-through; the stock fell from a 52-week high of DKK 556 to a low of DKK 220.6.
- Earnings: beat 5 of 7 quarters on consensus, but for a biotech that mostly reflects cost timing and milestone recognition.
- **Reliability: Medium** - operationally reliable on dates, promotional on efficacy framing.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS
- Amylin-class differentiation (Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs questions 2026-02-19) - deflected as "too early".
- Dose-titration logic and where tolerability gains come from - answered with Phase 1b reasoning, not data.
- Cash runway and spend - management stopped guiding on runway in 2025 and has not reinstated it, even as Phase 3 costs (shared with Roche) start.
- Why restart a GIP program it had deprioritised - framed as combination optionality.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS
- Red: Phase 2 petrelintide weight loss (about 9-11% at 28 weeks) sits well below the 15-20% target and well below Lilly's eloralintide, which runs roughly a year ahead.
- Red: survodutide's 18% stomach-related discontinuation in SYNCHRONIZE-2 (2026-10-01) undercuts the "better treatment experience" message for the royalty asset.
- Red: no runway guidance; trailing free cash burn about DKK 1.8 billion and rising with Phase 3.
- Red: scope creep (Boston hub, AI platform, small molecules) during the proof year.
- Green: balance sheet of about DKK 17-18 billion of cash and receivables against a market value of about DKK 17.5 billion.
- Green: Roche is co-funding a three-trial, roughly 7,000-patient Phase 3 program started 2026-09-22 - a large partner voted with its money after seeing the Phase 2 data.
- Green: remaining milestones (Roche and EUR 315 million from Boehringer) plus survodutide royalties of high-single to low-double digits.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS
- "Balanced partnership" is repeated deliberately: management wants investors to see Zealand as a co-owner, not a royalty vehicle - which also means Zealand carries half the development cost.
- The new emphasis on "proprietary data" and AI is a hedge against the core asset being a fast follower rather than a leader.
- The pivot of IR spokesman and the absence of rare-disease discussion suggest the rare-disease franchise is being de-prioritised.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)
**Trajectory: PIVOTING** - from a cash-funded stand-alone developer to a partner-funded co-owner entering an expensive Phase 3. The single most important thing to weigh: at DKK 249.60 the market is paying close to zero for the pipeline, but the cash is committed development funding that will be spent over the next three to four years, so the real question is whether petrelintide and survodutide are worth more than about DKK 6-8 billion of future spend. That is a probability-weighted pipeline bet with a cash cushion, not a classic value floor.

**Moat:** intangible (patents and partnership contracts). Narrow: there are no marketed products, returns are negative (return on invested capital about minus 25%), and competitors (Lilly's eloralintide, Novo's amycretin) are ahead in the amylin class. The trend is stable rather than eroding - nothing structural has removed the IP; the issue is competitive position, not a shrinking base. **Secular threat:** manageable - no structural force (AI displacement, reimbursement compression) threatens the terminal value specifically; obesity drug pricing pressure is a real but industry-wide risk. The cheapness is a fear-print about data quality and competition, not a structurally shrinking business.

Management credibility 3 of 5 · trajectory turning · a narrow but real moat · moat trend steady · structural threat manageable.
thesis_evidence: The thesis - a balance sheet that covers most of the market value plus partner-funded late-stage obesity assets - is corroborated by the latest dated numbers: cash and securities DKK 14.46 billion and Roche receivable DKK 3.82 billion against DKK 0.41 billion debt at 2026-06-30 (H1 2026 report); petrelintide Phase 3 started 2026-09-22 with Roche co-funding; survodutide Phase 3 positive in SYNCHRONIZE-1 (June 2026) and SYNCHRONIZE-2 (2026-10-01). The October readouts (2026-10-01 and 2026-10-07) were already priced into the 2026-10-19 committee answer. No new company fact has emerged since then; the Q3 2026 report is due 2026-11-12. The 7% price rise since the last look (DKK 233.80 on 2026-10-12 to DKK 249.60 on 2026-11-10) is a status update, not new information.
macro_fit_note: The backdrop is reflation (growth up, CPI about 3.7% a year through September 2026) in the discipline phase of the debt cycle, where positive real long rates punish long-dated stories and reward cash flow now, with an expected horizon of about 18 months. Zealand is a long-duration pipeline story burning cash, so the backdrop is a headwind, softened only by the large interest-earning cash pile. Inflation resilience cannot be measured from its accounts (no meaningful cost of sales); no pass-through evidence in the transcript.

bull_thesis: The market is paying close to nothing for two late-stage obesity drugs. At DKK 239.80 (FMP live quote, 2026-11-16) Zealand is valued at about DKK 15.9 billion, while at 2026-09-30 it held DKK 13.51 billion of cash and securities and DKK 4.19 billion of receivables (mostly Roche) against DKK 0.48 billion of debt - about DKK 15.3 billion, or DKK 231 a share, after current liabilities and the last tranche of the buyback. For an enterprise value (market value minus net cash) near zero, you own a 50/50 US and European profit share in petrelintide, an amylin analog (a copy of a gut hormone that makes people feel full) that Roche chose to take into a global three-trial Phase 3 program in September 2026 after seeing both Phase 2 trials, plus the same profit share on its combination with Roche's enicepatide (Phase 2 starting Q4 2026). Petrelintide's edge is tolerability: stomach-related dropouts of 1.5% versus 0% on placebo in ZUPREME-1 and 1.9% versus 1.7% in ZUPREME-2 - a profile management calls 'easy to start, and easy to stay on' (Q3 2026 call), in a market where, per the 2026-02-19 call, only a small fraction of patients exposed to GLP-1 drugs stay on them. Second, Zealand earns royalties and up to EUR 315 million of open milestones on Boehringer's survodutide, whose Phase 3 program is now complete: 16.6% weight loss in SYNCHRONIZE-1 (June 2026), up to 13.1% in diabetics (2026-10-01) and confirmed cardiovascular safety (2026-11-09), with filings in 2027 and liver-disease (MASH) data in 2027 that could widen its use. Third, management is disciplined with the cash: it bought back DKK 1.3 billion of stock at about DKK 295 (completed 2026-10-05) and guided 2026 costs to the low end of its range (2026-11-12). Conditions: Roche stays committed, Phase 3 pushes petrelintide toward the low-to-mid teens with placebo-like tolerability, survodutide is approved in 2027-28, and spending stays near DKK 2.5-3 billion a year.
bear_thesis: The cash is spoken for, and the drugs are second-tier. The screener's 2.7x price-to-free-cash-flow, 70% net margin and DKK 522.8 discounted-cash-flow value capitalise one-off Roche payments: recurring revenue was DKK 4 million in Q3 2026, trailing free cash flow is minus DKK 1.53 billion and return on invested capital is about minus 25%. Petrelintide missed management's own 15-20% target twice - about 10.7% at 42 weeks in ZUPREME-1 and up to 9.2% at 28 weeks in diabetics - and the Q3 2026 call quietly replaced the target with 'double-digit weight loss'. Lilly's eloralintide is about a year ahead with stronger numbers and Novo is advancing amylin drugs of its own, so tolerability may be a feature of the class, not of Zealand's molecule. Survodutide passed its heart-safety test, but about one in five patients stopped treatment for stomach side effects (2026-11-09), so it enters a crowded GLP-1 market as a liver-focused niche product. Meanwhile management is widening the spending agenda - a Cambridge research hub, an AI-protein collaboration, small molecules, '10 clinical programs by 2030' - and has never quantified its share of Phase 3 costs. If spending runs at DKK 2.5-3 billion a year for four years and both drugs prove commercially marginal, the stock converges on spent-down cash of about DKK 135 a share. What would confirm it: Roche scaling back Phase 3, competitor amylin data that clearly beat petrelintide, a survodutide approval delay, or 2027 cost guidance above DKK 3.3 billion.
consensus_delta: Where we disagree with the market: after a slide from a 52-week high of DKK 556 to DKK 239.80, the market prices Zealand as if its pipeline were worth roughly nothing and its cash will simply be burned. We agree the petrelintide data were below management's own target and that Lilly leads the amylin class. But the street is underweighting three dated facts: Roche committed to a full global Phase 3 after seeing all the data; survodutide has cleared every Phase 3 hurdle including heart safety (2026-11-09) and heads to filing in 2027; and management returned DKK 1.3 billion through a buyback while guiding costs to the low end. The screener's own signals (2.7x price-to-free-cash-flow, DKK 522.8 discounted-cash-flow value) are wrong in the other direction - they capitalise one-off milestones - and we disregard them.
forcing_function: The catalyst - what forces the re-rating: no single hard date. Nearest items are the start of the petrelintide plus enicepatide Phase 2 (Q4 2026), the full-year report and 2027 guidance (around February 2027), Boehringer's survodutide filings and MASH data (2027), and petrelintide Phase 3 data (about 2028). A new buyback funded from surplus cash, a milestone payment, or a licensing deal for the rare-disease assets would also narrow the gap between price and net cash.
valley_of_death: The risky window (the months just ahead): there is no debt wall and no liquidity risk, so this is a valuation-drawdown risk, not a solvency one. The main hazards are competitor amylin data from Lilly (eloralintide) and Novo at medical meetings, which can re-rate the whole class; 2027 cost guidance (due with the full-year report around February 2027) if it rises above about DKK 3.3 billion as Phase 3 and the research expansion ramp; and any sign that Roche is slowing the petrelintide program. Survodutide's tolerability (about 19-21% dropping out for stomach effects in the outcomes trial) could trim regulators' or prescribers' enthusiasm, but its value is a small part of ours.
positioning_washout: Forced-selling pressure has largely played out: the stock is down about 57% from its 52-week high, sits about 20% below its 200-day average of DKK 298.6 and only about 9% above its 52-week low of DKK 220.6. Momentum and growth funds that held it as an obesity proxy have been leaving since the first Phase 2 readout in early 2026. There is no dividend base to liquidate and no index event identified; further selling would be fundamental (data or spending), not mechanical. The company's own buyback at about DKK 295 shows management saw value well above today's price.
moderator_conclusion: Buy now. The thesis holds and the news since our last look on 10 November 2026 nudged it slightly in our favour: Boehringer's survodutide passed its heart-safety trial on 9 November and will be filed in 2027, and the 12 November quarterly report showed DKK 13.5 billion of cash and securities plus DKK 4.2 billion of receivables, with 2026 costs guided to the low end of the range - the spending scare we flagged did not happen. At DKK 239.80 you pay about DKK 15.9 billion for a company with roughly DKK 15.3 billion of net cash and receivables, and you get a half share of Roche's petrelintide program and a royalty on survodutide for very little. Correcting the share count for the October buyback (about 66.3 million shares) and lifting survodutide's odds roughly offset, so our base-case fair value is DKK 300 a share, about 25% above the price and clear of our 20% bar for buying in today's reflationary market. This is not a classic value floor: the cash is committed to an expensive Phase 3 and a widening research agenda, petrelintide's weight loss missed management's own target, and Lilly leads the class. So conviction stays moderate (3 of 5), the value case scores 3 of 5, and the debt-cycle backdrop, which punishes long-dated stories, is a headwind. Watch 2027 cost guidance and competitor amylin data.
sop_fair_value: DKK 300 a share (base case), against a live price of DKK 239.80, inside a wide band from about DKK 135 (adverse) to DKK 575 (favorable).
sop_breakdown: Net cash, securities and receivables less debt, current liabilities and the October buyback tranche (2026-09-30 balance sheet): about DKK 15.3 billion, DKK 231 a share on about 66.3 million shares; less about 18-24 months of shared Phase 3 and research spend (about DKK 3.5-4 billion, DKK 57 a share) = about DKK 174. Petrelintide 50% profit share plus open Roche milestones, risk-weighted at about 30-35% and discounted: about DKK 5.6 billion, DKK 84 a share. Survodutide royalties plus EUR 315 million of milestones, risk-weighted at about 70% after the cardiovascular result and with a haircut for tolerability: about DKK 2.75 billion, DKK 42 a share. Early pipeline: nil in the base case. Total about DKK 300 a share.
risk_reward: Downside to the adverse case of about DKK 135 against upside to the base-case fair value of DKK 300 and a favorable case of DKK 575; the pipeline computes the ratios from these levels. The asymmetry is moderate, not deep: the downside case assumes the cash is spent and both drugs disappoint.
peer_comps_note: Peers (Viking, Gubra, Altimmune, Structure, Novo Nordisk, Lilly, Roche) are not comparable on earnings multiples because Zealand has no product earnings; the peer file's own read is that headline cheapness from milestones overstates the gap. The cleaner yardstick is enterprise value: Zealand trades near zero enterprise value once Roche receivables are counted, while US obesity pure-plays with earlier or comparable assets carry positive multi-billion-dollar enterprise values. On that basis Zealand is cheap versus peers, though part of the discount is deserved because petrelintide trails Lilly's eloralintide. No peer override multiple was supplied and none is cited from memory; the peer file flags no shared regulatory driver. No FMP analyst price targets exist for this listing and none are used.
interrogator_dossier:
# Zealand Pharma (ZEAL.CO) - a deep dive on management and the setup

*Prepared 2026-11-16. Quote used: DKK 239.80 on the Copenhagen listing (FMP live quote, 2026-11-16). Transcripts read: Q1 2025 (2025-05-09), H1 2025 (2025-08-14), Q3 2025 (2025-11-13), full year 2025 (2026-02-19) and Q3 2026 (2026-11-12). The Q1 and H1 2026 calls were not in the bundle, so the 2026 readouts between February and November are reconstructed from the Q3 2026 call and the dated company announcements.*

**Bottom line.** Zealand is a clinical-stage peptide company whose stock is now worth less than the cash and partner receivables on its balance sheet net of near-term liabilities, plus a modest value for two late-stage obesity programs run with Roche and Boehringer Ingelheim. Management has hit nearly every timeline it set, but the clinical numbers have landed below the 15-20% weight-loss bar it set for its lead drug. The reported profits and the screener's 2.7x price-to-free-cash-flow are one-off milestone artifacts and should be ignored.

## 1. Narrative arc

- **Q1 2025 (2025-05-09):** the story was the newly signed Roche deal - "historic and transformative" - a 50/50 profit share on petrelintide (an amylin analog, a copy of a gut hormone that makes people feel full) in the US and Europe. The pitch: a better-tolerated alternative to GLP-1 drugs, targeting 15-20% weight loss.
- **H1 2025 (2025-08-14):** two leading programs (petrelintide and survodutide, Boehringer's glucagon/GLP-1 drug on which Zealand earns royalties). Amylin pitched as "the next major class". Rare-disease assets and dapiglutide still part of the story.
- **Q3 2025 (2025-11-13):** dapiglutide paused ("the GLP-1-based therapeutic space has become increasingly crowded"). The company narrowed to its two partnered obesity assets and talked of becoming "a generational biotech".
- **Full year 2025 (2026-02-19):** "the most defining and catalyst-rich year" in the company's history; a Boston research hub, AI-driven discovery, "more than 10 candidates into the clinic" in five years, and "5 product launches over the next 5 years".
- **Q3 2026 (2026-11-12):** the language moved from weight-loss magnitude to "first-choice" and "easy to start, and easy to stay on". The research story widened again: a Cambridge (US) hub, a Generate Biomedicines AI-protein deal, small molecules via OTR, and a "multimodality metabolic health company". The rare-disease assets (dasiglucagon, glepaglutide) are now to be licensed out.

The arc is a pivot from a single-asset partnership story to a platform story, with the efficacy target quietly reframed from "15% to 20%" to "double-digit weight loss" with placebo-like tolerability.

## 2. Claims vs financials (forensic)

| Claim | Evidence | Read |
|---|---|---|
| "Secured enough capital to fund our journey towards profitability" (Q1 2025) | Cash and securities DKK 13.51bn and DKK 4.19bn of receivables against DKK 0.48bn of debt at 2026-09-30 (FMP statements). Down from DKK 15.11bn at end-2025, partly due to a roughly DKK 1.3bn share buyback completed 2026-10-05. | Holds. No financing risk for years. |
| Earnings strength (screener: net margin 70%, P/FCF 2.7x, EPS 90.22 in 2025) | 2025 revenue DKK 9.21bn and 2026 Q2 revenue DKK 4.49bn are Roche upfront and milestone payments. Recurring revenue was DKK 34m in Q1 2026 and DKK 4m in Q3 2026; TTM free cash flow is minus DKK 1.53bn; return on invested capital about minus 25%. | Does not hold. The cheapness on earnings is an artifact. |
| Cost discipline | 2026 operating-expense guidance DKK 2.7-3.3bn; on 2026-11-12 the CFO said guidance was narrowed "to the lower end". Q3 2026 net operating loss only DKK 54m after cost sharing. | Holds; burn is running below the feared DKK 3bn+. |
| Petrelintide 15-20% weight loss (Q3 2025, FY 2025) | ZUPREME-1: "up to 10.7% mean weight loss at week 42", GI discontinuation 1.5% vs 0% placebo. ZUPREME-2 (diabetics): up to 9.2% at week 28, A1c down up to 0.65 points (Q3 2026 call). | Missed the stated efficacy target; the tolerability claim held. |
| Survodutide competitive weight loss, comparable tolerability (Q3 2025) | SYNCHRONIZE-1 16.6% (June 2026), SYNCHRONIZE-2 up to 13.1% in diabetics (2026-10-01), SYNCHRONIZE-CVOT met cardiovascular safety (2026-11-09, AHA). Press reports put GI discontinuations around 19-21% in the outcomes trial. Boehringer confirmed global filings in 2027. | Efficacy and safety hold; tolerability is worse than management implied. |
| Five launches in five years | Glepaglutide received a positive opinion from the EU medicines committee (CHMP) in Q3 2026; survodutide filing 2027; petrelintide Phase 3 started 2026-09. | On track in part; rare-disease launches will be via out-licensing. |

## 3. Tone and confidence trajectory - Stable to slightly declining

- Q1 2025: "never been in a stronger position" - maximum confidence.
- H1 2025 and Q3 2025: still bold on targets ("We remain fully confident in the potential of petrelintide to deliver 15% to 20% weight loss in Phase III").
- FY 2025: "catalyst-rich year"; success defined as data reinforcing "approximately 15% to 20%".
- Q3 2026: no restatement of the 15-20% figure; replaced by "double-digit weight loss" and "a tolerability profile that is generally comparable to placebo". The CFO declined to say where cost savings came from.

Confidence on execution stays high; confidence on the efficacy number has been walked back. That is a defensive shift dressed in offensive language.

## 4. Guidance credibility - Medium

Delivered: ZUPREME-1 data in the first half of 2026 (guided Q1); Phase 3 start in the second half of 2026 (started 2026-09); ZUPREME-2 in the second half of 2026; combination Phase 2 (ZYNERGY, with Roche's enicepatide, formerly CT-388) now guided to Q4 2026 versus "first half of 2026" on 2026-02-19 - a slip of about two quarters. Operating expenses inside guidance. Missed: the efficacy target. Dasiglucagon manufacturing has been delayed repeatedly by a third-party facility. Timelines are reliable; outcome claims are not. The screener's 5-of-7 earnings beat rate is meaningless for a company whose revenue is milestone timing.

## 5. Analyst pressure points

- Tolerability versus efficacy trade-off in amylins (Wells Fargo, Q3 2025; Danske, H1 2025 on the flat dose response in men). Management answered with the 480-patient Phase 2 - which then showed about 10.7%.
- Survodutide GI tolerability (UBS, Q3 2025): management promised "comparable" tolerability; the outcomes trial showed about one in five stopping for GI effects.
- Cost sharing with Roche and caps on spend (Goldman, Q1 2025): never quantified; "we are not yet providing clear guidance".
- Where cost savings came from (BNP Paribas, Q3 2026): not answered.
- Competitive position versus Lilly's eloralintide and Novo's amycretin and cagrilintide: always deflected with "best-in-class potential", never with head-to-head data.

## 6. Red flags / green flags

Red flags
- The 15-20% weight-loss target set in 2025 and reaffirmed on 2026-02-19 was not met in either Phase 2 trial; the Q3 2026 call no longer quotes it.
- Survodutide GI discontinuations of about 19-21% in the outcomes trial (reported 2026-11-09) contradict "comparable tolerability" (Q3 2025).
- Scope creep during the proof years: Boston/Cambridge hub, AI-protein collaboration, small molecules, "10 clinical programs by 2030" - spending that competes with returning cash.
- The combination Phase 2 slipped from the first half of 2026 to Q4 2026.
- Stock-page earnings, margins and DCF value are built on one-off milestone payments.

Green flags
- Roche - which saw all the Phase 2 data - started a roughly three-trial global Phase 3 program in 2026-09 and is co-funding it; a sophisticated partner voting with money.
- Survodutide's Phase 3 program is complete, cardiovascular safety is confirmed (2026-11-09) and Boehringer has committed to filing in 2027, which de-risks royalties and the remaining milestones.
- Placebo-like GI discontinuation for petrelintide in both Phase 2 trials (1.5% vs 0% and 1.9% vs 1.7%).
- Capital discipline: a DKK 1.3bn buyback at about DKK 295 (completed 2026-10-05) and 2026 costs guided to the low end.
- Positive EU committee opinion for glepaglutide in short bowel syndrome.

## 7. Hidden signals

- "End the weight loss Olympics" (Q3 2025) became the frame that pre-justified a sub-target result: the bar was moved before the data arrived.
- CT-388 is now called enicepatide - Roche is branding its own asset, a small sign the combination is a Roche priority.
- New voices: the Chief Scientific Officer (Utpal Singh, ex-Lilly) now speaks on every call and the platform narrative is his; investor relations changed hands (Eric Rojas replaced Adam Lange in 2026). The scientific voice talks of "polypharmacology" and China access - a broader, more expensive ambition.
- Management now says the rare-disease assets will be licensed, not commercialized - a quiet retreat from building a commercial organization.
- "Without relying on dilutive funding" was added to the Q3 2026 framing - reassurance that suggests investors have asked.

## 8. Capital-allocation verdict

Trajectory: **PIVOTING** - from a partnership-milestone company to a platform research company, funded by a cash pile that today exceeds the market value of the equity net of liabilities. The single most important thing the director must weigh: the stock is a claim on about DKK 230 a share of net cash and receivables that management intends to spend, not return. The value case works only if (a) petrelintide earns a real share of the amylin market despite trailing Lilly on efficacy, or (b) management keeps returning surplus cash as it did in 2026. The buyback is the best evidence for (b).

**Moat.** Type: intangible (patented peptide molecules and 25 years of peptide know-how), validated by two big-pharma partners. Width: narrow - there are no product earnings, returns on capital are negative, and the tolerability edge looks like a property of the amylin class that Lilly and Novo share. Trend: stable - the patent estate and partner terms are unchanged; the competitive position neither widened nor collapsed in 2026.

**Secular threat.** None of the listed structural forces (AI displacement, disintermediation, reimbursement compression and so on) threatens the terminal value directly. The real risk is competitive and clinical - Lilly's and Novo's amylin programs and price competition in obesity - which is manageable, not terminal. The cheapness is a fear print around below-target data, not a structurally shrinking base, but the cash cushion is being consumed by design.
